name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q01 - Classification of allylic alcohols and phenol

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In allylic alcohols, the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is attached to an \(sp^3\)-hybridised carbon atom adjacent to a carbon–carbon double bond.

Statement II: In phenol, the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is directly attached to an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon atom of an aromatic ring.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alcohols and phenols are classified according to the hybridisation of the carbon atom to which the hydroxyl (\(-\mathrm{OH}\)) group is bonded.

Step 2: Evaluation
In allylic alcohols (such as \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH}\)), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is bonded to an \(sp^3\)-hybridised carbon atom next to a \(\mathrm{C=C}\) double bond (an allylic carbon), so the first claim is true. In phenol (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}\)), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is directly bonded to an \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon atom of the benzene ring, so the second claim is also true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q02 - Boiling points of ethanol methoxymethane and branched alcohols

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ethanol has a significantly higher boiling point than methoxymethane of comparable molecular mass due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

Statement II: The boiling point of isomeric alcohols increases with an increase in branching of the carbon chain.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Boiling points depend on the strength of intermolecular forces, including hydrogen bonding and van der Waals dispersion forces.

Step 2: Evaluation
Ethanol (\(\mathrm{b.p.\ 351\ K}\)) forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds, whereas methoxymethane (\(\mathrm{b.p.\ 248\ K}\)) lacks \(\mathrm{O-H}\) hydrogen bonding; hence, the first claim is true. However, in isomeric alcohols, increasing branching makes the molecule more compact, decreasing surface area and weakening van der Waals forces, which lowers the boiling point (e.g., butan-1-ol boils higher than butan-2-ol). Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q03 - Acid catalysed hydration vs hydroboration oxidation of propene

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Acid-catalysed hydration of propene yields propan-1-ol as the major product.

Statement II: Hydroboration–oxidation of propene using diborane followed by hydrogen peroxide in aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) yields propan-1-ol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acid-catalysed hydration of unsymmetrical alkenes follows Markovnikov's rule via the more stable carbocation, whereas hydroboration–oxidation gives net anti-Markovnikov addition of water.

Step 2: Evaluation
Acid-catalysed hydration of propene proceeds through the secondary propyl carbocation (\(\mathrm{CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3}\)) to give propan-2-ol as the major product, making the first claim false. In contrast, hydroboration–oxidation attaches boron to the less substituted terminal carbon and subsequently replaces it with \(-\mathrm{OH}\) to give propan-1-ol in excellent yield, making the second claim true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q04 - Preparation of phenol from chlorobenzene and cumene

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Chlorobenzene is converted into sodium phenoxide by fusing with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(298\text{ K}\) and \(1\text{ atm}\) pressure.

Statement II: In the commercial manufacture of phenol from cumene, methanol is obtained as a major by-product.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleophilic substitution on aryl halides requires drastic conditions, and industrial manufacture of phenol from cumene involves oxidation to cumene hydroperoxide followed by acid cleavage.

Step 2: Evaluation
Chlorobenzene requires drastic conditions of \(623\text{ K}\) and \(300\text{–}320\text{ atm}\) pressure to fuse with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) and form sodium phenoxide, not \(298\text{ K}\) and \(1\text{ atm}\); hence, the first claim is false. In the cumene process, acid-catalysed cleavage of cumene hydroperoxide yields phenol and acetone (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\)) as the by-product, not methanol; hence, the second claim is also false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q05 - Acidity of phenol and effect of nitro substituents

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Phenol is a much stronger acid than ethanol because the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance delocalisation of negative charge over the aromatic ring.

Statement II: The presence of an electron-withdrawing nitro group at the ortho or para position enhances the acidic strength of phenol.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acid strength depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed upon deprotonation.

Step 2: Evaluation
In the ethoxide ion (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5O^-}\)), the negative charge is localised on the oxygen atom, whereas in the phenoxide ion (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5O^-}\)), the negative charge is delocalised over the benzene ring through resonance, making phenol about a million times more acidic than ethanol; thus, the first claim is true. Furthermore, an electron-withdrawing \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\) group at the ortho or para position effectively delocalises and stabilises the negative charge of the phenoxide ion via \(-I\) and \(-R\) effects, increasing acidity; thus, the second claim is also true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q06 - Nitration of phenol and steam volatility of nitrophenols

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas p-nitrophenol is less volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

Statement II: Direct nitration of phenol with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) in nearly \(100\%\) yield.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intramolecular hydrogen bonding prevents molecular association and increases volatility, whereas intermolecular hydrogen bonding causes association and lowers volatility. Strong oxidising acids like concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) can oxidise activated aromatic rings like phenol.

Step 2: Evaluation
o-Nitrophenol exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding and is therefore steam volatile, whereas p-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds leading to molecular association and lower volatility; hence, the first claim is true. However, direct nitration of phenol with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) gives picric acid in poor yield due to extensive oxidation of phenol (modern synthesis converts phenol to phenol-2,4-disulphonic acid first); hence, the second claim is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q07 - Williamson synthesis limitation and SN1 cleavage of tert-butyl ether

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Heating tert-butyl chloride with sodium ethoxide is an efficient method to prepare tert-butyl ethyl ether via Williamson synthesis.

Statement II: Heating tert-butyl methyl ether with concentrated \(\mathrm{HI}\) yields tert-butyl iodide and methanol via an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Williamson synthesis requires \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) attack of an alkoxide on a primary alkyl halide; with tertiary alkyl halides, strong alkoxide bases cause elimination. Cleavage of tertiary alkyl ethers with \(\mathrm{HI}\) proceeds via an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) pathway governed by carbocation stability.

Step 2: Evaluation
Reacting tert-butyl chloride with sodium ethoxide leads predominantly to elimination, forming 2-methylprop-1-ene rather than tert-butyl ethyl ether; thus, the first claim is false. On the other hand, protonation of tert-butyl methyl ether followed by slow loss of methanol generates the stable tertiary carbocation \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C^+}\), which rapidly combines with \(\mathrm{I^-}\) to give tert-butyl iodide and methanol; thus, the second claim is true.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q08 - Action of heated Cu on tertiary alcohol and PCC oxidation of allylic alcohol

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Passing vapours of 2-methylpropan-2-ol over heated copper at \(573\text{ K}\) yields 2-methylpropanal by dehydrogenation.

Statement II: Oxidation of \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2OH}\) with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) cleaves the double bond to produce ethanoic acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Heated copper at \(573\text{ K}\) dehydrogenates primary and secondary alcohols but dehydrates tertiary alcohols. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild, selective oxidising agent for converting primary alcohols to aldehydes.

Step 2: Evaluation
2-Methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol lacking an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen; over heated \(\mathrm{Cu}\) at \(573\text{ K}\), it undergoes dehydration to form the alkene 2-methylpropene, not 2-methylpropanal, making the first claim false. Meanwhile, PCC selectively oxidises \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2OH}\) to the \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CHO}\) without cleaving the \(\mathrm{C=C}\) double bond or over-oxidising to a carboxylic acid, making the second claim also false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
